passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: Business Strategy Cintas helps more than one million businesses of all types and sizes, primarily in the U.S., as well as Canada and Latin America, get READY™ to open their doors with confidence every day by providing a wide range of products and services that enhance our customers’ image and help keep their facilities and employees clean, safe and looking their best. With products and services including uniforms, mats, mops, shop towels, restroom supplies, workplace water services, first aid and safety products, eye-wash stations, safety training, fire extinguishers, sprinkler systems and alarm services, Cintas helps customers get Ready for the Workday ® . We are North America's leading provider of corporate identity uniforms through rental and sales programs, as well as a significant provider of related business services, including entrance mats, restroom cleaning services and supplies, first aid and safety services and fire protection products and services. Cintas' principal objective is "to exceed customers' expectations in order to maximize the long-term value of Cintas for shareholders and working partners," and it provides the framework and focus for Cintas' business strategy. This strategy is to achieve revenue growth for all our products and services by increasing our penetration at existing customers and by broadening our customer base to include market segments to which we have not historically served. We will also continue to identify additional product and service opportunities for our current and future customers. To pursue the strategy of increasing penetration, we have a highly talented and diverse team of service professionals visiting our customers on a regular basis. This frequent contact with our customers enables us to develop close personal relationships. The combination of our distribution system and these strong customer relationships provides a platform from which we launch additional products and services. We pursue the strategy of broadening our customer base in several ways. Cintas has a national sales organization introducing all its products and services to prospects in all market segments. Our broad range of products and services allows our sales organization to consider any type of business a prospect. We also broaden our customer base through geographic expansion. Finally, we evaluate strategic acquisitions as opportunities arise. Results of Operations This Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations section focuses on discussion of fiscal 2026 results compared to fiscal 2025 results and should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the related notes included elsewhere in this filing. The discussion contains forward-looking statements that involve known and unknown risks and uncertainties, including those set forth under " Item 1A. Risk Factors ." For discussion of fiscal 2025 results compared to fiscal 2024 results, see the "Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” within our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended May 31, 2025, filed with the SEC on July 28, 2025. Cintas classifies its business into two reportable operating segments and places the remainder of its operating segments in an All Other category. Cintas’ two reportable operating segments are Uniform Rental and Facility Services and First Aid and Safety Services. The Uniform Rental and Facility Services reportable operating segment consists of the rental and servicing of uniforms and other garments including flame resistant clothing, mats, mops and shop towels and other ancillary items. In addition to these rental items, restroom cleaning services and supplies and the sale of items from our catalogs to our customers on route are included within this reportable operating segment. The First Aid and Safety Services reportable operating segment consists of first aid and safety products and services, as well as workplace water services. The remainder of Cintas’ business, which consists of the Fire Protection Services operating segment and the Uniform Direct Sale operating segment, is included in All Other. These operating segments consist of fire protection products and services and the direct sale of uniforms and related items. Cintas evaluates operating segment performance based on revenue and operating income. Revenue and operating income for the reportable operating segments for the fiscal years ended May 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024 are presented in Note 14 entitled Operating Segment Information of "Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements." The Company regularly reviews its operating segments for reporting purposes based on the information its chief operating decision maker (CODM) regularly reviews for purposes of allocating resources and assessing performance and makes changes when appropriate. 23 On March 10, 2026, the Company entered into a Merger Agreement pursuant to which the Company will acquire all outstanding shares of UniFirst common stock. UniFirst is a North American company in the supply and servicing of uniform and workwear programs, facility service products, as well as first aid and safety supplies and services. Under the terms of the Merger Agreement, subject to the satisfaction (or, to the extent permitted by applicable law in accordance with the Merger Agreement, waiver) of certain conditions, Cintas will acquire all the outstanding shares of UniFirst common stock in a transaction valued at approximately $5.5 billion. credit_strengths.text: Cintas generates substantial recurring revenue from uniform rental and facility services, with an operating margin well above the consumer discretionary sector median, reflecting pricing power and route density. Operating income has grown steadily over the past three fiscal years, supporting strong internal cash generation and consistent profitability.

Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditures, producing free cash flow that exceeds total debt by a wide margin. This cash conversion strength, combined with minimal net leverage, provides significant financial flexibility and supports the company's investment-grade-like credit profile.

key_risks.text: The pending acquisition of UniFirst, valued at approximately five and a half billion dollars, introduces integration and execution risk. The transaction requires regulatory approvals and may strain management resources, while the assumed debt and cash consideration could temporarily elevate leverage above current minimal levels.

A significant portion of debt matures within the next twelve months, including senior notes due in the following fiscal year. Although the company has a revolving credit facility and commercial paper program, refinancing this amount at higher rates could increase interest expense and pressure coverage metrics.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage remains exceptionally strong, with operating income covering interest expense many times over. This ample cushion, combined with a high proportion of fixed-rate senior notes, limits near-term earnings volatility from rate movements and supports consistent debt service.

Free cash flow to debt is robust, and the company retains substantial undrawn revolver capacity. However, the upcoming maturity wall will require refinancing or repayment, and the UniFirst acquisition could absorb a meaningful portion of liquidity, warranting close monitoring of post-deal leverage.

overall_credit_view.text: Cintas exhibits a minimal indicative financial risk profile, with net leverage well below the sector median and cash flow coverage ratios that rank in the top quartile. The company's scale, recurring revenue model, and disciplined capital allocation support a strong credit standing.

The UniFirst acquisition is a key swing factor; if completed, leverage may rise temporarily, but the combined entity's cash generation should restore metrics. Absent the deal, credit metrics are expected to remain stable, with shareholder returns consuming a large share of free cash flow.

credit_strengths.text: Cintas 從制服租賃及設施服務產生大量經常性收入，其營業利潤率遠高於非必需消費品行業中位數，反映其定價能力及路線密度。過去三個財政年度，營業收入穩步增長，支持強勁的內部現金生成及持續盈利能力。
經營現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，產生的自由現金流大幅超過總債務。此現金轉換實力，加上極低的淨槓桿，提供顯著的財務靈活性，並支持公司類投資級的信用狀況。

key_risks.text: 待完成的 UniFirst 收購，價值約五十五億元，帶來整合及執行風險。該交易需要監管批准，並可能對管理資源造成壓力，而承擔的債務及現金代價可能暫時將槓桿推高至目前極低水平之上。
相當部分債務將於未來十二個月內到期，包括下一個財政年度到期的高級票據。儘管公司擁有循環信貸融資及商業票據計劃，以較高利率為此金額再融資可能增加利息支出並對覆蓋率指標構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率仍然異常強勁，營業收入覆蓋利息支出多倍。此充裕緩衝，加上高比例固定利率高級票據，限制了利率變動對近期盈利的波動，並支持持續償債。
自由現金流對債務比率穩健，且公司保留大量未提取的循環信貸額度。然而，即將到期的債務牆將需要再融資或償還，而 UniFirst 收購可能吸收相當部分流動性，值得密切監測交易後的槓桿。

overall_credit_view.text: Cintas 顯示極低的指示性財務風險狀況，淨槓桿遠低於行業中位數，現金流覆蓋率位居最高四分位。公司的規模、經常性收入模式及嚴謹的資本配置支持強勁的信用狀況。
UniFirst 收購是關鍵搖擺因素；若完成，槓桿可能暫時上升，但合併後實體的現金生成應可恢復指標。若無此交易，信用指標預計保持穩定，股東回報將消耗大部分自由現金流。
